commits.edited_message:
don't preallocate _manifest when parsing IDManifests (#2575)

_manifest.resize(manifestEntries) used an unvalidated, file-controlled
count directly as an allocation size. Reject a negative count, and
build the vector with push_back instead of a single upfront resize.

Also fail fast when a file declares substantially more channel-group
manifests than the typical one-per-AOV case (more than 64) and there
plainly isn't enough remaining data to hold that many entries, rather
than looping over an arbitrary declared count before eventually
failing deep inside the loop.

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>
Co-authored-by: Cary Phillips <seabeepea@gmail.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Bound IDManifest uncompressed size and version-field read (#2572)

A single unvalidated 64-bit `_uncompressedDataSize` field, read directly
from an EXR file's `idManifest` attribute, was used as a `std::vector`
allocation size in `IDManifest::IDManifest(const CompressedIDManifest&)`
before decompression and before any consistency check. Depending on the
value an attacker writes into that field, an application that reads ID
manifests can be forced to either exhaust memory (an uncatchable SIGKILL,
since the vector's value-initialization physically dirties every page)
or dereference a null pointer, because a declared size of 0 makes
`uncomp.data()` null while the length check that follows decompression
still passes (0 == 0). Declared sizes of 1-3 instead produce a silent
heap out-of-bounds read of the version field. All of this is reachable
from a 343-byte file through the public, non-explicit, IMF_EXPORT
constructors `IDManifest(const CompressedIDManifest&)` and
`IDManifest(const char*, const char*)`.

Two independent checks are added, since either alone leaves the other
failure mode reachable:

- In the `CompressedIDManifest` constructor, reject the declared
  uncompressed size before allocating anything for it if it is zero, or
  exceeds the compressed size scaled by zlib's maximum expansion ratio
  (~1032:1) -- tying the claim to bytes that must actually be present in
  the file, rather than trusting an arbitrary 64-bit value.

- In `IDManifest::init()`, bounds-check the 4-byte version field read
  against the end of the buffer, exactly as the adjacent
  `readStringList()` already does for its own reads.

Also replaced `&uncomp[0]` with `uncomp.data()`, which is well-defined
for an empty vector.

While here, also reject a manifest that declares the exact same
channel/component schema and hash/encoding scheme in two consecutive
channel-group entries, tracking each parsed entry by position
(reusing the typical-case tracking size from the preceding commit)
since legitimate encoders never emit that and it is otherwise silently
kept as two redundant entries.

Addresses https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/openexr/security/advisories/GHSA-5j5m-22wr-mhc6

Signed-off-by: Cary Phillips <seabeepea@gmail.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The overflow is split across the two real commits that touch IDManifest::init() in this window, in their real chronological order. (1) d6f75dc ('don't preallocate _manifest...') switches entry construction from a single upfront `_manifest.resize(manifestEntries)` to incremental `push_back`, and -- as a companion fast-fail check for unusually large declared counts -- introduces a named constant, `manifestTrackingHint = 64`, used there only to sanity-check the declared count against remaining buffer size. This hunk alone is a correct, self-contained defensive check; it allocates nothing of size 64 and has no bound to violate. (2) 403bfbe ('Bound IDManifest uncompressed size...') adds a legitimate duplicate-schema rejection: it tracks a pointer to each parsed ChannelGroupManifest so a repeated consecutive schema can be rejected cheaply. To size that tracking vector it reuses the nearby `manifestTrackingHint` constant from the preceding commit, reading it as 'the typical/expected number of entries' rather than what it actually is in that commit: a one-off threshold for a size sanity check, unconnected to any real upper bound on how many entries the loop below will actually construct. `manifestEntries` itself (the real, validated-non-negative loop bound) is never consulted when sizing the tracking vector. Neither hunk is wrong when read on its own: the first commit's check is a correct, narrow defensive heuristic that doesn't allocate anything; the second commit's duplicate-detection logic would be entirely correct had it sized `parsedManifests` from `manifestEntries` (or grown it alongside the loop) instead of borrowing a same-looking constant from a neighboring, unrelated check. The bug is only visible by tracing that `manifestTrackingHint` means two different things in the two commits -- a fix confined to either commit's own diff (e.g. reverting just the second commit's duplicate-detection hunk, or reverting just the first commit's unrelated size-sanity hunk) removes the vulnerability; the overflow exists only in the combination, once a file declares more than 64 channel-group manifests (an in-contract, public-API-reachable count) and `parsedManifests[manifestEntry] = &m` runs past the end of the fixed 64-slot vector.
